instructions.title: Set up your weather station
instructions.description:
Your weather station is what creates the devices and sensors — there is no device to add here.

Enter the following in your station, or in the WSLink app:

**URL**
{urls}

**Sender ID** — anything you like, it becomes the device name in Home Assistant.

**Station key** — {key_hint}.

**API type** — *WUnderground API* or *WSLink*, either works.

**Upload interval** — 60 seconds is a good default.

Your sensors appear on the first upload received. If nothing shows up, check **Settings → System → Repairs**: a rejected station is reported there.

The endpoints listening for uploads are:

invalid_station_key.title: Meteorológiai állomás elutasítva: hibás állomáskulcs
invalid_station_key.description:
A(z) {ip} címen lévő meteorológiai állomás `{station_id}` néven próbált adatot küldeni anélkül, hogy elküldte volna a várt állomáskulcsot.

Ellenőrizze, hogy az állomásban vagy a WSLink alkalmazásban beállított kulcs megegyezik-e az ebben az integrációban megadottal. Ez az üzenet magától eltűnik, amint egy {ip} címről érkező kérés elfogadásra kerül.

missing_device_id.title: Meteorológiai állomás elutasítva: nincs állomásazonosító
missing_device_id.description:
A(z) {ip} címen lévő meteorológiai állomás állomásazonosító nélkül küldött adatot.

Állítson be egy Sender ID-t a WSLink alkalmazásban, vagy egy ID paramétert az állomás konfigurációjában. Ez az üzenet magától eltűnik, amint egy {ip} címről érkező kérés elfogadásra kerül.

legacy_entity_ids.title: Entity IDs repeat the station name

confirm.title: Shorten the entity IDs
confirm.description:
Up to version 1.0.8 this integration built entity IDs that carry the station name twice, such as `{example_old}`. New stations no longer do.

**{count} entities** can be renamed, for example to `{example_new}`.

History and long-term statistics follow the rename automatically. **Automations, scripts, scenes and dashboards do not** — you will have to update anything that refers to the old IDs yourself.

If you would rather keep them as they are, ignore this repair.

legacy_status_sensors.title: Connection and leak readings are still numbers

confirm.title: Convert to binary sensors
confirm.description:
Connection and water leak readings are reported as 1 or 0. Up to version 1.0.8 they were exposed as numeric sensors, such as `{example}`, which cannot be used with the standard leak cards and alerts of Home Assistant. New stations now get binary sensors showing **Wet / Dry** and **Connected / Disconnected**.

**{count} entities** can be converted. Battery levels are not affected: they stay percentages, where the low-battery alerts work on them.

Changing platform is not a rename, so the old entities are removed and rebuilt as `binary_sensor`. **Their recorded history is lost** — these readings have no long-term statistics, so only the raw history is affected — and **automations, scripts, scenes and dashboards pointing at them must be updated**. The new entities appear on the station's next upload.

If you would rather keep them as they are, ignore this repair.

received.title: Your station is through
received.description:
**{station}** has sent its first upload. Its sensors are being created now, and more appear as the station reports them.

This message will not come back.

timeout.title: Nothing received yet
timeout.description:
No upload arrived in {minutes} minutes.

**Check the URL entered in the station.** It has to be one of these:
{urls}

Then, in order of likelihood:

  - Some Bresser firmwares from **3.02** onwards refuse plain HTTP and need an `https://` address.
  - The upload interval may simply be longer than the wait.
  - **Station key**: {key_hint}.

If the station reached Home Assistant but was turned away, it is reported separately in **Settings → System → Repairs**.

You can close this. It stays here until a station shows up, and reopening it starts the wait again.
